      World 01 / E1 · The Maze

      Same task. Same model. Same route?

      A goal can have several valid paths. An agent chooses which calls to make—and repeated attempts need not make the same choices.

      9 models20 graphs30 trials per pairing5,400 trials

      Meet the playing field.

      A graph connects operations to the resources they require and produce. Some routes branch and rejoin. Others enforce a long chain. We repeat the same task with the same model thirty times and compare the attempted call sequences.

      The graph structure comes from public API specifications; execution uses anonymized operations in a benchmark, rather than live production services.

      PREDICT → REVEAL

      If all thirty attempts take one route, are they reliable?

      Change the model. Then change the maze.

      Metrics below describe the selected model × graph pairing. Open the heatmap to compare every pairing, then click any cell to replay its paths.

      Averages leave out the setting.

      A model can look consistent on a constrained graph and variable on one with choices. The entropy decomposition below describes the eight-model analysis; the interactive results above include all nine models, including Opus.

      These are shares of the fitted entropy decomposition, not causal effects. The residual includes interactions and sampling variation.
